info.title: Firebird API
info.description: Control plane API for bare-metal servers, virtual machines, networking, storage, and identity management.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description:
Audit log API.
Filter by tenant_id, trace_id, correlation_id, target_kind, target_id, related_kind, related_id — each filter is independent and combined with AND

- Troubleshoot who did what and when

Pagination:
- Cursor-based using pageSize and pageToken

Tip:
- Provide from_ts/to_ts for defining the date range for best performance and predictable results

tags.name: Operations
tags.description:
Async Operation tracking API.

Asynchronous mutations return an Operation that can be polled for progress; an endpoint's response schema determines whether an operation must be polled (synchronous mutations return their resource directly).

- GET /operations/{id} returns current status
- GET /operations lists operations for the tenant

tags.name: Bare Metal
tags.description:
Bare-metal server lifecycle operations.

Includes:
- List and get bare-metal servers
- Provision operations
- Power on/off, reboot
- Attach / detach bare-metal servers to subnets

All endpoints require a Bearer token (Authorization header).

tags.name: Network
tags.description:
Network (VPC) API.

Use this section to:
- Create and manage VPCs within a project
- Manage subnets under a VPC
- Manage firewall rules for network traffic control

Common fields:
- project_id scopes all operations
- vpc_id scopes subnet operations

Notes:
- state reflects lifecycle (PROVISIONING/READY/ERROR/DELETING)

Pagination:
- List endpoints use limit and offset

tags.name: Storage
tags.description:
Storage (Filesystem) API.

Use this section to:
- Create, update and delete project filesystems
- List filesystems within a project
- Retrieve filesystem details and access credentials

Common fields:
- project_id scopes all operations
- id identifies a filesystem

Notes:
- total_capacity is specified in GB
- state reflects lifecycle (PROVISIONING/READY/UPDATING/ERROR/DELETING)

Pagination:
- List endpoints use limit and offset

tags.name: Images
tags.description:
Image API.

Use this section to:
- List OS/application images available within a scope
- Retrieve image metadata (name, version, architecture, size)
- Upload large image files using a server-mediated multipart upload flow

Resource model:
- Images are scoped by a typed resource ID in the URL: `tenant.ULID` or `project.ULID`
- Tenant-scoped images are visible to all projects under that tenant
- Project-scoped images are visible only within that project (plus tenant images)
- tenant_id is derived from the bearer token; clients do not pass tenant_id in requests
- Storage internals (URL, checksum, bucket/object paths) are not exposed in API responses

Upload flow (server-mediated multipart):
1) StartImageUpload — declare the file (name, size, content type) and receive:
   - upload_id (session identifier)
   - part_size_bytes (use for every part except the last)
   - max_in_flight_parts (recommended concurrency)
2) Upload parts — upload each part by part_number:
   - gRPC clients: Not supported for gRPC API, use REST API instead.
   - REST clients: PUT /compute/images/{scope_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/parts/{part_number} with raw binary body
3) GetImageUploadStatus — optional; returns uploaded parts to support resume/retry
4) FinishImageUpload — validates contiguous parts (1..N) and total size; returns object_id
5) AbortImageUpload — cancels an in-progress upload and frees server-side resources

Pagination:
- List endpoints use cursor-based pagination (page_size + page_token)

tags.name: Machine Types
tags.description:
Hardware profile catalog for bare-metal servers.

Machine types define the hardware specifications (CPU, memory, GPU, storage, network) of bare-metal servers. Use these endpoints to discover available hardware profiles and query capacity.

All catalog endpoints are public (no authentication required). The capacity summary endpoint requires authentication.

tags.name: Network ACL
tags.description:
Subnet Network ACL API.

A Network ACL is a named set of allow rules attached to exactly one subnet. It is the only mutable property of a subnet — name, CIDR and gateway are fixed at creation.

Notes:
- No ACL means all traffic is allowed
- Adding the first rule in a direction switches that direction to default-deny
- Rules also filter traffic between workloads inside the same subnet

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Projects API.

Use this section to:
- Create and manage projects used to group compute, network and storage resources
- List projects available to the current tenant

Notes:
- project id is referenced across other APIs as project_id

Pagination:
- List endpoints use limit and offset

tags.name: IAM
tags.description:
Identity and Access Management API.

Key rules:
- Tenant is implicit from JWT.
- Creating a user or service account grants NO roles by default.
- Roles are granted only via explicit role-binding endpoints.
- Tenant ADMIN can manage all users, service accounts, and role bindings in a tenant.
- Project ADMIN can manage project-level role bindings within that project.

post.description:
Obtain an access token using one of the supported grant types:

**password** — for users. Provide `email` and `password`.

**client_credentials** — for service accounts. Provide `client_id` and `client_secret`.

**refresh_token** — rotate an expiring access token. Provide the `refresh_token` returned by a previous Token call. 

Returns a JWT access token that must be included in all subsequent requests as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.description: Returns the subnet's Network ACL. A subnet with no ACL returns 200 with network_acl absent — that is the default state and permits all traffic. 404 means the subnet itself was not found.

put.summary: Create or replace a subnet's network ACL
put.description: Sets the subnet's complete rule set and initiates the async push to the network layer. Idempotent upsert: the whole ACL is always submitted, since the network layer rewrites the entire rule set on every change and there is no way to patch one rule in isolation. A single invalid rule rejects the whole request. Note that adding the first rule in a direction switches that direction to default-deny, and that rules also filter traffic between workloads inside the same subnet.

400.description: Invalid request (bad CIDR, malformed port list, ports on a protocol that has none, unsupported network backend)

post.summary: Invite a user to the tenant
post.description:
Creates a pending invitation for an email to join the tenant. The invitee is always granted tenant ADMIN on accept — the role is not caller-selectable (the request's `role` field is reserved and ignored). Tenant membership and the ADMIN role are granted when the invitee accepts. Requires tenant ADMIN.

For organization tenants the invitee's email domain MUST be one of the tenant's VERIFIED domains, otherwise the request is rejected with 403.

Idempotency: a second invitation for an email that already has a pending invitation in this tenant returns 409.

403.description: Insufficient permissions, unverified tenant, or email domain not verified for this organization

409.description: A pending invitation for this email already exists

delete.description: Revokes a pending invitation by deleting the invitation record. Requires tenant ADMIN.

post.description: Resets the invitation's expiry to a fresh 7-day window. Requires tenant ADMIN.

cidr.description: Optional IPv4 CIDR block within RFC 1918 private space (10.0.0.0/8, 172.16.0.0/16, or 192.168.0.0/16). Prefix length MUST be one of /8, /16, or /24 — reverse-DNS zones (in-addr.arpa) require byte-aligned prefixes so downstream DNS ops can own each zone cleanly. Examples: 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 192.168.1.0/24.
